Each day the gate stays open is a day the hold cannot lift for a reason that is one table and one route away, and no third-party status-page account is needed to close it.
user_persona: Three (PRD User stories): (1) a stranger's agent reading `/status.json`'s `state`/incident title before retrying; (2) the operator, opening/updating/closing incidents in one call each and citing one 90-day uptime number per component; (3) mcphost-deploy, posting an external probe via `admin.status.sample` so the page reflects outside-in reachability too.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given the host has run for 3 minutes, When GET /status.json is called anonymously, Then it returns state: "operational", four components each with a last_sample within 90s, and Cache-Control: max-age=60.
Given the sandbox executor is disabled in the test harness, When 5 sample ticks pass, Then components[exec].state is "failing" and state is "degraded".

Given admin.incident.open {title, impact: "major", components: ["mcp"]}, When /status.json is called, Then state is "outage", the incident appears in incidents_open, and admin_audit holds the open entry.

Given an open incident, When admin.incident.update {id, message} then admin.incident.close {id, message} run, Then the timeline has three entries in order and the incident moves to incidents_recent_30d.
Given 1,440 samples for one day with 1,425 ok, When the daily rollup runs, Then status_daily shows ok_samples: 1425 and /status.json reports uptime_30d computed from the rollup.

Given admin.status.sample {component: "mcp", ok: false, latency_ms: 0, source: "deploy-probe"}, When posted 5 times, Then the component's state reflects the external samples and source is preserved per row.
Given samples older than 90 days, When the daily prune runs, Then they are deleted and the rollup rows for those days remain.
Given www/status.html is served, When the page loads with /status.json reachable, Then it renders the four components and incident list; when the fetch fails, the static fallback text is visible.

Given the alerting registry is present and a component fails 5 consecutive samples, When the tick runs, Then one status.component_down alert is raised and an incident with impact: partial is open; after 10 ok samples it is closed with a timeline note.
Given GET /status.json?component=mcp&days=7, When called, Then seven daily rows with ok_samples, total_samples, p95_latency_ms return.

Given prod after land, When https://mcphost.dev/status.json is fetched, Then it returns operational with four components and status.html renders it (Live; evidence: mcphost-1 healthz version after deploy plus the call transcript, saved under docs/receipts/<slug>.md).

additional.self_samples_never_touch_calls_or_meteri: Technical considerations: 'the self samples call the same handler functions the HTTP layer dispatches to, in process ... they must not count in calls or metering' -- probe_mcp checks db writability plus self_check_tools_list() (the same anonymous tools/list construction, called directly, no RequestContext/HTTP); probe_exec calls the python Kind's own call() through a hand-built CallCtx under a dedicated status-feed-self-check namespace; probe_billing signs and replays a synthetic event through billing::process_webhook; probe_claim calls claim::resolve_claim_token directly. None of the four opens a socket to this host's own listener or writes a calls/meter_events row.
additional.exec_absent_python_kind_counts_as_failin: AC2's own premise ('the sandbox executor is disabled in the test harness') maps directly onto this crate's existing KindRegistry::with_builtin(), which registers only echo -- probe_exec treats kinds.get("python") returning None as an outright failing sample (ok: false, latency_ms: 0), not a skipped/N-A one, so AC1's test must explicitly register the python kind (python_kind_registry) to see exec read ok, exactly the same registration AC2's default TestServer omits to see it read failing.
additional.billing_probe_is_trivially_ok_when_uncon: PRD-grand-loop-billing goal 4 already treats an absent Stripe key as the supported 'billing is off' state -- probe_billing follows the same precedent: no MCPHOST_STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET configured means there is no webhook route behavior to probe, so it reads ok: true rather than manufacturing a failure a host that never turned billing on can do nothing about.
additional.component_state_and_overall_state_are_bi: requirement 3's own language ('every component's last 5 samples are ok' / 'one failing component') never names a per-component degraded state, only ok/failing -- component_state() returns exactly those two strings (never-sampled counts as failing), and overall_state() layers outage (major-impact open incident or every component failing) / degraded (partial-impact open incident or any one component failing) / operational on top, matching AC1-AC3's wording precisely.
additional.probe_overrides_is_the_ac9_test_lever_no: AC9 needs one component to flip from failing to ok deterministically inside one running server without a real subprocess crash or a 15-real-minute wait; AppState.status_probe_override (empty in every real `mcphost serve` start) is that lever, following the exact 'field, not process environment, since tests run in parallel in one binary' rule this crate already applies to alert_config/sandbox_mechanism/deprecations -- it is read once per component per tick, before the real probe would otherwise run, and never reachable from any admin.* tool.
additional.auto_incidents_only_auto_close_incidents: requirement 6 says a component-down incident auto-closes after 10 consecutive ok samples, but does not say what happens to a human-opened incident that happens to name the same component -- incidents.auto (0 for admin.incident.open, 1 for the tick's own open_auto_incident) scopes close_auto_incident to auto: true rows only, so an operator's own incident is never silently closed out from under them; only a mechanism-opened one is.

five_whys_trace.q: Why build a self-reported status feed now, rather than signing up for a third-party status-page account?
five_whys_trace.a: Readiness gate 6 ('Instatus status page') has sat open on Joe's to-do list since the market-test-plan wiki page (2026-09-23), alongside the email provider and DMCA registration; scout confirmed healthz has no history table at all. Each day the gate stays open is a day the launch hold cannot lift for a reason that costs one table and one route, and no vendor account is required to close it -- a machine-readable feed the host computes from its own probes satisfies the same gate at zero external dependency.

five_whys_trace.q: Why sample four fixed components every minute from inside the process, rather than reusing the existing /healthz check?
five_whys_trace.a: Requirement 2's own four probes (mcp initialize+tools/list, exec through the sandbox path, billing's webhook route, claim's invalid-token refusal) each exercise a materially different failure surface healthz's single db/disk_ok boolean never distinguishes -- AC2 specifically needs exec's own state to diverge from mcp/billing/claim's, which a single aggregate healthz bit cannot express.

five_whys_trace.q: Why gate operator incidents behind admin.incident.{open,update,close} rather than writing directly to a status_daily-adjacent table by hand?
five_whys_trace.a: User stories: 'admin.incident.open {title, components, impact} publishes an incident in one call; update adds a timeline entry; close sets resolution' -- and requirement 4 ties every one of those writes into admin_audit, the same accountable trail every other admin.* mutation in this crate already gets (AC3/AC4 both assert on it).

five_whys_trace.q: Why let 5 consecutive self-sample failures auto-open an incident and auto-raise an alert, rather than requiring an operator to notice and open one by hand?
five_whys_trace.a: Requirement 6's own non-functional companion metric -- 'time from component failure to public status change: never -> <=5 min' -- cannot be met by a human noticing; wiring the existing alerting registry (PRD-mcphost-alerting-webhook, this PRD's own Depends-on) to auto-open a partial-impact incident is the mechanical way to guarantee that ceiling without paging anyone to do it by hand.

five_whys_trace.q: Why keep status_daily rows forever while pruning raw status_samples after 90 days, rather than pruning both the same way?
five_whys_trace.a: Goal: '90-day uptime per component is one number per day I can cite in the launch post' -- the operator's own use case (citing a 90-day, or later a lifetime, uptime number) only ever needs the rolled-up daily aggregate, never the individual per-minute sample; keeping the aggregate forever while bounding the much higher-volume raw table is the same 'aggregate survives, raw data ages out' shape this crate's own calls/meter_events retention split already established (PRD-mcphost-data-retention).
